decisions.reason: As a generic utility outside the firm’s core regulated-energy specialization, this option likely revealed limited strategic value by 2022 and is easy to abandon in favor of higher-fit platform products.
This database is close to the firm’s existing market-data strengths, extends its energy-domain coverage, and can be kept open at relatively low incremental cost while demand develops.
The service fits the firm’s regulatory and analytical niche well, so real-options logic favors retaining it because uncertainty can still resolve positively without heavy additional commitment.
An end-customer tariff database is adjacent to the firm’s data and software base, so despite some market uncertainty it remains worth keeping as a plausible platform component.
Custom web services are useful but not very product-like, so management would likely fold this into general service work rather than keep it as a distinct market offering.

A postal code lookup service is a commoditized, weakly differentiated tool with limited connection to the firm’s core energy-process advantage, making abandonment likely once its option value is tested.
